results.Title: A TPM 2.0 is present, enabled and owned
results.Detail: The control threw during evaluation: The property 'TpmPresent' cannot be found on this object. Verify that the property exists.
results.Rationale: BitLocker binds its volume key to a measured boot state held in the TPM. Without a usable TPM 2.0 the boot volume cannot be protected and every measurement-based control above it is decoration.

results.Title: UEFI Secure Boot is enabled
results.Detail: Unable to set proper privileges. Access was denied.
results.Rationale: Secure Boot stops a modified bootloader from running underneath the operating system. It is a prerequisite for the measured launch the rest of the trust stack depends on, and it cannot be retrofitted without a rebuild.

results.Title: Security baseline drift control is enabled
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzsSecurity' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: Drift control re-evaluates the protected baseline settings every 90 minutes and reverts anything that changed. Without it the baseline is a one-time hardening pass that decays, and a loosened setting stays loosened.

results.Title: Virtualization-Based Security is enabled
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzsSecurity' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: VBS is the hypervisor-enforced memory boundary that Credential Guard and HVCI are built on. Neither of those controls means anything without it.

results.Title: Hypervisor-protected code integrity is enabled
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzsSecurity' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: HVCI verifies that every kernel-mode driver is signed and unmodified before it runs, which closes an entire category of rootkit.

results.Title: Credential Guard is enabled
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzsSecurity' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: Credential Guard isolates derived credentials so that compromising a host does not hand an attacker reusable hashes to pivot with. It is the control that keeps one compromised node from becoming a domain compromise.

results.Title: Dynamic Root of Trust for Measurement is enabled
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzsSecurity' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: DRTM establishes a clean measured launch environment after boot, so a firmware-level compromise no longer poisons everything downstream. Instances deployed before the 2504 release may still be on the older static root of trust.

results.Title: Side channel mitigations are enabled
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzsSecurity' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: Speculative execution mitigations matter more on a hypervisor than anywhere else, because the boundary being attacked is the one between tenant workloads.

results.Title: SMB signing is enabled for external traffic
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzsSecurity' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: SMB signing prevents tampering and relay attacks on traffic leaving the cluster. Changing it does not need a reboot, though existing sessions keep the previous setting until they reconnect.

results.Title: SMB encryption is enabled for in-cluster traffic
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzsSecurity' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: East-west storage traffic between nodes carries workload data in clear text unless cluster encryption is on. Measure the throughput cost before enabling it on a latency-sensitive cluster, but measure it rather than assuming it.

results.Title: Application Control is in Enforced mode
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AsWdacPolicyMode' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: Audit mode logs what would have been blocked and then allows it to run anyway. A cluster left in audit mode has the paperwork of application control with none of the protection, which is the single most common finding on a mature deployment.

results.Title: Every WDAC supplemental policy is on the approved list
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-ASLocalWDACPolicyInfo' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: Supplemental policies are how third-party agents are allowed to run, and each one widens the trust boundary. An undocumented supplemental policy is an unreviewed exception, and it is exactly what breaks during an update.

results.Title: Every boot volume is BitLocker encrypted
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-ASBitLocker' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: An unencrypted boot volume means a stolen or RMA-returned disk hands over the operating system, its configuration and any cached material on it.

results.Title: Every Cluster Shared Volume is BitLocker encrypted
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-ASBitLocker' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: Volumes created after deployment do not inherit encryption. A CSV added six months into the cluster life is the usual gap, and it is the volume with the workload data on it.

results.Title: BitLocker recovery keys are retrievable for every node
results.Expected: At least one recovery key per node
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AsRecoveryKeyInfo' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: The platform escrows keys to Active Directory or Key Vault, which is a fine default until the disaster you need them for is the one that took out the directory. If this check cannot enumerate a key per node, your recovery path is untested.

results.Title: Microsoft Defender real-time protection is active
results.Detail: If a non-Microsoft antivirus is in use instead, confirm it is ISV-validated for Azure Local and that the documented exclusion paths are configured.
results.Rationale: Defender Antivirus ships enabled and configured. If real-time protection is off, something turned it off, and that is worth knowing about.

results.Title: Defender signatures are current
results.Rationale: A cluster with stale signatures is usually a cluster that lost its outbound path to Microsoft Update, which means several other things are probably also failing quietly.

results.Title: Potentially unwanted application protection is enforced
results.Detail: A value of 2 is audit mode: detections are logged but nothing is blocked.
results.Rationale: PUA blocking was added to the Defender settings in the 2506 baseline. It catches the bundled remote-access and crypto-mining tooling that is technically legitimate and never belongs on a hypervisor host.

results.Title: Syslog forwarding to a SIEM is enabled
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzSSyslogForwarder' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: Security events that never leave the cluster cannot be correlated, cannot be retained beyond the local log and cannot be investigated after an incident that took the cluster with it.

results.Title: Syslog forwarding uses TCP with TLS encryption
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzSSyslogForwarder' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: UDP and plain TCP send security events unauthenticated and in clear text. Those transports exist for lab testing and have a habit of surviving into production.

results.Title: Syslog forwarding uses mutual TLS authentication
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-AzSSyslogForwarder' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: Mutual authentication is the highest supported configuration and the only one where the collector can prove which node sent an event. Server-only authentication is acceptable; anything below it is not.

results.Title: The well-known RID 500 administrator account is disabled
results.Detail: Administrator (RID 500) is in the expected state.
results.Rationale: ASBuiltInAdmin is enabled by default and its SID is predictable, which makes it a free target for password spraying. Microsoft recommends creating a custom administrative account and disabling this one.

results.Title: The well-known RID 501 guest account is disabled
results.Detail: Guest (RID 501) is in the expected state.
results.Rationale: ASBuiltInGuest is disabled by default and drift control keeps it that way. If this check fails, either drift control is off or something re-enabled it deliberately.

results.Title: Minimum password length meets the baseline
results.Rationale: The 2607 baseline raised the local minimum password length to 14 characters to align with the Azure Security Baseline and NIST guidance. Systems built on an earlier release can still be sitting on the old default.

results.Title: An interactive logon legal notice is configured
results.Rationale: Both DISA STIG and CIS ask for a logon banner, and the 2604 baseline ships one. The settings are drift-protected, so customising the wording means disabling drift control first, changing it, then turning drift control back on.

results.Title: The solution update environment is healthy
results.Detail: The cmdlet 'Get-SolutionUpdateEnvironment' is not available. Run this on an Azure Local node, or install the module that provides it.
results.Rationale: The security baseline itself ships with the release. A cluster that has drifted off the release train is not just missing patches, it is running an older definition of what secure means.
